title: Anomalous Pairing Currents and a Second Topological Edge Channel in Bosonic Lattices
authors: Chitrak Bhadra, Ángel Rivas, Miguel A. Martin-Delgado
abstract: We show that bosonic pairing opens a second chiral current channel on a 2D kagome lattice, absent from any particle-conserving model. From the continuity equation, we derive both a hopping current and an anomalous pairing current on the lattice, and predict chiral circulation in bulk-gapped phases with integer para-unitary Chern numbers, as well as a phase-sensitive leakage ratio, $Λ_{\cal I}$, for the pairing current around a defect. This ratio can be tuned from confined to strongly anomalous regimes at fixed topology. The two channels differ microscopically: the hopping current is sourced by the on-bond single-particle coherence, whereas the pairing current is sourced by the off-site anomalous coherence, whose spatial range is governed by the BdG pairing gap rather than by the single-particle gap. This separation produces distinct defect-induced signatures in real space, identifies a regime in which bulk topology and anomalous edge response coexist with no analogue in particle-conserving matter, and is directly testable in driven photonic lattices and superconducting-circuit arrays.
summary: The paper investigates anomalous pairing currents in bosonic lattices on a kagome structure. It shows that these pairing currents create a second, distinct chiral current channel not found in particle-conserving theories. The key diagnostic tool is the phase-sensitive leakage ratio ($\Lambda_I$), which allows for experimental verification of this unique topological feature in circuit or photonic arrays.
main_problem: To establish a microscopic statement regarding the distinct topological contribution of anomalous pairing currents ($	ext{PC}$) in bosonic systems, which is absent in particle-conserving models.
main_result: Bosonic pairing opens a second chiral current channel ($\langle I angle$) distinct from the single-particle hopping current ($\langle J angle$), providing a unique topological signature testable in driven quantum platforms.
method: The analysis uses para-unitary diagonalization of the Bogoliubov Hamiltonian and derives lattice continuity equations to calculate both $	ext{SPC}$ and $	ext{PC}$.
model_or_system: The system is modeled on a 2D kagome lattice using bosonic operators, incorporating hopping terms (single-particle coherence) and pairing terms (anomalous coherence). The model is directly mapped onto superconducting circuits or photonic lattices.
key_observables: Single Particle Current ($\langle J angle$), Pairing Current ($\langle I angle$), Phase-sensitive leakage ratio ($\Lambda_I$), Integer para-unitary Chern numbers ($C_n$).

main_assumptions: The standard fermionic index theorem does not transfer literally because the diagonalization structure group is $U(m, m)$ rather than compact $U(2m)$.
figures_summary: Figures compare microscopic current decompositions ($	ext{SPC}$ vs $	ext{PC}$) around edges and defects for different phase configurations (Case 1, Case 2, Case 3).
paper_structure: The paper develops by first defining the full bosonic Hamiltonian, deriving separate continuity equations for hopping and pairing currents, analyzing topological invariants via para-unitary diagonalization, and finally comparing results across distinct physical regimes (anomalous vs. confined).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable diagnostic ($\Lambda_I$) to distinguish genuine topological physics in bosonic systems from standard fermionic models, which is crucial for interpreting measurements in superconducting circuits or photonics.
